BiblicalUsage: Adlai is named once, as the father of Shaphat, who was over David's herds in the valleys. That is the whole record — a father, a son, and a job in the king's service.
TheologicalSignificance: This name holds no doctrine, and I won't dress it up as one. It is a reminder that the kingdom ran on ordinary work — herds in the valleys, men to watch them — and the record kept the names of the families behind that work.
RelatedPeople: Adlai, Father of Shaphat; King David
